summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of polymyositis, morbid obesity, interstitial lung disease, diastolic heart failure, type 2 diabetes, and recurrent venous thromboembolism was admitted for diffuse muscle weakness concerning for a polymyositis flare. She had elevated CK and CRP, was treated with three days of IV methylprednisolone, then transitioned to oral prednisone and mycophenolate. Her weakness improved, and CK decreased. She also had acute on chronic heart failure with mild dyspnea and fluid overload, managed with IV lasix and optimization of home medications. Hypertension was worsened by steroids and addressed by increasing losartan. Warfarin was restarted after a period of underuse. She was started on Bactrim for PJP prophylaxis and metformin for steroid-induced hyperglycemia. She was discharged home on a new medication regimen with close follow-up planned with rheumatology and her primary care team.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
Body mass index [BMI] 70 or greater, adult
Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories
Hypertensive heart disease with heart failure
Personal history of other venous thrombosis and embolism
Patient's intentional underdosing of medication regimen for other reason
